With no tenant bound, erp_app sees 0 companies, branches, tenants and workplaces. Bound to alnoor, it sees 0 of B's companies and workplaces, its UPDATEs of B rows change 0 rows, and its INSERT into B is refused. SET ROLE postgres, DISABLE RLS and NO FORCE RLS are all refused. The new CHECK constraints are present: TRN ^[0-9]{15}$, Arabic name required under the setting, and recent ids at most 6.

biggest_gap.title: G2 checks which permission an endpoint declares, never what the endpoint writes: a company setting changed through PUT /api/tenancy/workplace (tenancy.workplace.switch only) passes every gate
biggest_gap.detail: Every tenancy endpoint declares a reviewed permission, and the gates attack that declaration thoroughly. No gate checks that a request authorised by permission P writes only the records P covers. I planted P1b in WorkplaceEndpoints.Switch: SwitchWorkplaceRequest gains `bool? ArabicLegalNameRequired`, and the handler sets it on the target company when the caller works in every branch of it. With that plant, any user who may switch company can switch on the company's Arabic-legal-name requirement, a legal setting that otherwise needs tenancy.companies.update. All 142 product gates passed, and the live product took the change. This is the 'every action is denied unless a role grants it' bar, broken inside an endpoint this piece owns. A UAE group gives every clerk the switch permission, so any such side door is open to the whole staff. Fix: give each permission a reviewed write set, for example tenancy.workplace.switch -> tenancy.user_workplaces only, and tenancy.companies.update -> tenancy.companies minus the logo columns. During G2's 'granting exactly one permission' run, read audit.entries by correlation id and fail any request under P that writes a table or column outside P's set. Add P1b to the gate self-tests.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/batchA2-L2b-P1b.diff applied at 322d0ef (the planted file is kept as plants/A2-WorkplaceEndpoints-planted.cs.txt). Run `dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName!~Erp.Gates.Tests.SelfTests"`: 142/142 pass (plants/batchA2-gates.log). Live: ERP_PROJECT=c-p02-tenancy-r10-plant ERP_HTTP_PORT=20270 ERP_DB_PORT=20271 ERP_SEED_VOLUME=2000 ./erp up, then node plants/P1b-live2.mjs http://localhost:20270. other_findings: [route: p00-foundation] The G1 source gate (G1TenantSourceTests, ignore-tenant-filter rule) misses the tenant query filter switched off when the filter names are passed in a variable. Plant L2b: `string[] ownRow = [ModuleDbContext.CompanyFilterName, ModuleDbContext.TenantFilterName]; db.Workplaces.IgnoreQueryFilters(ownRow)` in WorkplaceEndpoints.Get. The rule's regex matches only `IgnoreQueryFilters()` or a call that names TenantFilterName or "tenant" inside its parentheses. Both full gate runs passed with it (batchA-gates.log, batchA2-gates.log). RLS still held, so nothing leaked, but CLAUDE.md rule 1's second layer was gone unnoticed. Suggested fix: flag any IgnoreQueryFilters whose argument is not a literal list of reviewed non-tenant filter names, or check the filters EF actually applies at run time.
